lesson_title: Brick, Wall, Room, House, Street: How 30 Trillion Cells Become You
hook_text: An Amoeba does every job with one cell. You have 30 trillion cells and almost every one does only one thing.
clip_script: An Amoeba in a pond is one cell doing everything: eating, moving, breathing, making copies. One-person spaza shop. You are a big company: 30 trillion workers, one job each. That is division of labour, and because each cell does one job, it can be shaped for it. Red blood cell: flat, dented, no nucleus, so it is packed with haemoglobin to carry oxygen. Muscle cell: long, full of mitochondria, because pulling takes energy. Nerve cell: a wire up to a metre long so the message does not get passed along. Root hair cell: a long finger into the soil for more surface to soak up water. Feature, then job. Now stack them. A brick is a cell. A wall of the same bricks is a tissue. Walls plus a floor plus a roof make a room, an organ, like the heart. Rooms make a house, a system. The street is you. Cell, tissue, organ, system, organism. And the blank bricks that have not decided yet? Stem cells, in your bone marrow, making new blood for life.
visual_style: A single wobbling Amoeba splits into a crowd of differently shaped cells, each snapping into its job; bricks stack into a wall, a room, a house and a street; one brick glows blank and divides.
mood: Energetic, clear, building to a reveal.
pacing: Quick contrast at the start, four punchy cell beats, a steady five-step climb to the street.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the feature-then-job sentence for any cell they give you.
